claims.text: Structural and chemical stability is governed by formation of a stable surface oxide layer.
The surface oxide layer acts as a barrier to further oxidation and degradation.
High entropy of mixing enhances formation of a homogeneous oxide layer.
High entropy of mixing increases the diffusion rates of the constituent elements.
Increased constituent diffusion promotes formation of a stable, defect-free oxide structure.
The initial Fe20Co30Cr20Ni20Mn10 nanoalloy has an FCC structure.
The initial nanoalloy has an average grain size of 10 nm.
Heating at 800°C produces a stable surface oxide containing iron, cobalt, chromium, nickel, and manganese oxides.
High-temperature conditions facilitate oxygen diffusion to the surface and reaction with the alloy elements.
The oxide barrier stabilizes both the structure and composition of the nanoalloy.
The stable oxide layer will reduce the oxidation rate by 30% relative to the baseline.
The oxidation rate will decrease from 0.1 to 0.07 mg/cm²/h.
The oxidation rate in the absence of the stable oxide layer is 0.1 mg/cm²/h.
The prediction remains valid at temperatures up to 900°C.
The prediction applies across Fe20-40Co20-40Cr10-30Ni10-30Mn5-15 compositions.
The stated composition range satisfies the requirement for high entropy of mixing.
The upper temperature boundary is determined by stability of the oxide layer and nanoalloy structure.

contradictions.description: The experiment specifies only a controlled argon atmosphere, while the proposed mediator and mechanism require an oxygen supply. No oxygen partial pressure, impurity level, or deliberate oxidizing exposure is specified.
